transportBoundaryPolicy.sendMeaning: Confirmation sending has an explicit local handoff-confirm-a/b event before the send-confirm-a/b remote delivery event. ownConfirmationSent changes at handoff only. The reciprocal sender becomes usable at handoff after peer verification, while the reply is still in flight.
transportBoundaryPolicy.receiveMeaning: send-confirm-a/b delivery effects change only receiver.receivedConfirmation. Receiver.peerConfirmed and usable require a separate verify-confirm-a/b event.
transportBoundaryPolicy.negativeMeaning: First sender handoff occurs in negative paths too. Rejection never creates the reciprocal confirmation or any usable key. No error packet is invented.

spake2.name: SPAKE2
spake2.implementation: Standards-based teaching profile; no live implementation claim
spake2.supportStatus: standards-based teaching profile; not an AD, Keycloak or browser feature
spake2.group: P-256; cofactor 1; RFC fixed M and N; uncompressed SEC1 points
spake2.kdf: HKDF-SHA256; nil salt; info ConfirmationKeys concatenated with empty AAD; 32 output bytes split into 16-byte KcA and KcB
spake2.transcript: len(A)||A||len(B)||B||len(pA)||pA||len(pB)||pB||len(K)||K||len(w)||w; lengths uint64 little-endian; w fixed-width 32-byte big-endian
spake2.setup: Official vector supplies w, x and y directly; MHF/password mapping omitted by RFC vector. Synthetic password input is an explanatory handle, not a claimed derived vector password.
spake2.export: Ke is first 16 bytes of SHA256(TT); Ka is remaining 16; Ka and KcA/KcB confirmation-only
spake2.ordinaryTransport: Abstract ordered unprotected teaching transport; RFC does not define framing or a transport binding
omissions: No production randomness or runtime cryptographic implementation
No application data format, authorization, KDC, ticket, cookie or OAuth token
No packetization or network retransmission policy
